newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs might be invited in 1997 to join NATO - Havel.
newsitem.headline: Czechs might be invited in 1997 to join NATO - Havel.

text.p: The Czech Republic might be invited this summer to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO), President Vaclav Havel said on Sunday.

"Everything suggests that certain countries... including the Czech Republic... might be directly invited at the summer summit in Madrid, and the process of admitting new NATO members would thus be launched," he said in a regular radio speech.
His remarks followed a meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl who came to Prague to sign a long expected declaration on Czech-German reconciliation last Tuesday.
"I noticed a certain progress in the determination to start negotiations on the enlargement of NATO," Havel commented on his meeting with Kohl. He said Kohl supported the process unambiguously.
But Havel added he did not think there was any direct connection between the signing of the Czech-German declaration and the chances of the Czech Republic joining European structures.

The latest opinion poll taken by the private polling agency Factum in early December showed that only 37 percent of 1,074 respondents agreed with Czech membership of NATO while 55 percent wished to join the European Union.
